title: Does a player's horn tell his message? Herbie Fields's playing
summary: Dance wonders whether Fields was frustrated by his playing lacking feeling and Cobb agrees that a player expresses what is on his mind through his horn.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: You don't think, though, (inaudible), you know, that he wanted to be sort of jazz player, and that he was so dissatisfied with what he'd accomplished. I mean I've heard him on records, and I thought, well, anybody like that that wants to play and is -- in a sense he's mastered the horn, but he can't say anything, that must be hard for him. You know, if he want --
In other words, you're saying he didn't send out a message.
He just played -- well, I'll grant you that, and I'm very agreeable with that. I think anybody blew a horn, they could tell what they got on their mind through
their horns, and you can feel it out there. And you can.
I mean a lot of those things he did (inaudible) he just sounds very corny.
